blogs.title: Unleashing GPU Power: How FlashAttention‑3 Turns Attention into Lightning Speed
blogs.description: The attention layer has long been the performance choke‑point in transformers—especially when models need to remember thousands of tokens. This post breaks down what makes attention expensive, why previous optimizations (FlashAttention‑2) were limited on modern GPUs, and how FlashAttention‑3’s warp‑specialized design lets the hardware’s Tensor Cores and Tensor Memory Accelerator work in tandem for massive speedups.

blogs.title: Inside the Pipeline: Overlapping Softmax and Matrix Multiplication for Turbocharged Attention
blogs.description: Softmax calculations are tiny compared to huge matrix multiplications yet can stall throughput on GPUs. Here we dive into FlashAttention‑3’s two‑stage pipeline that shuffles workers between computing Q×K·T and applying softmax so both steps run simultaneously—like juggling blocks with a relay race strategy.

blogs.title: FP8 on GPUs: Making Low‑Precision Attention Accurate
blogs.description: FP8 promises twice the raw compute but at higher numerical cost. Learn how Block Quantization + Incoherent Processing (random orthogonal mixing) let FlashAttention‑3 keep error low while locking in fast FP8 GEMM performance—making high‑speed attention practical for training large language models.

blogs.title: From Theory to Practice: Benchmarks Show FlashAttention‑3 Outperforms Industry Standards
blogs.description: Numbers speak louder than code. This article walks through real benchmarks comparing FlashAttention‑3 (FP16/FP8) against baseline PyTorch attention, earlier FlashAttention versions, and NVIDIA cuDNN kernels—highlighting up to 2× speedups and near 75 % GPU utilization on Hopper H100 cards.

blogs.title: Building Faster Language Models for Long Contexts: Why Hardware‑Aware Algorithms Matter
blogs.description: Long‑context applications—from multi‑document reasoning to code completion—need supercharged attention layers. Explore how hardware features like Hopper’s asynchronous TMA/WGMMA units drive algorithmic innovations such as FlashAttention‑3, paving the way for richer, real‑time language model experiences.
